messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: compare decay rates
parts:
Sacha:

I presume that because you want to know if there is geographic variation
in your decay rates, you are using the 'retrospective' method of
estimating decay (Laing et al. 2003). That method fits a logistic
regression to your data. I don't know more about the number of regions
you have, but assuming you have a small number of them (and replicates
within each region), you could consider adding a 'region' as a factor to
your logistic regression and trying to make inference on the region
coefficients.

If you are R-savvy, take a look at the lovely exercise that Mike
Meredith of WCS Malaysia has put together on estimating decay rates
using the retrospective method
(http://www.wcsmalaysia.org/analysis/Nest_dung_decay.htm); that may be
of use to you.

messages.author: 6919d512766fa133
messages.subject: Re: compare decay rates
parts:
Sacha:

I wish to give one more suggestion for the analysis of data relating
to decay rate. I had an opportunity to analyze the data of dung decay
experiments conducted following Laing et al. (2003) in connection with
the population estimation of elephants. However, it was observed from
the detailed analysis that the data collected were not found to follow
the logistic regression model. So, we had to resort to alternative
statistical technique for analysis. We used Kaplan-Meier survivorship
function (Hosmer and Lemeshow 1999) for estimating average survival
time of the dung piles (referred to as time to decay). The
Kaplan-Meier survival analysis is free of models (non-parametric).
Log-rank test (non-parametric) was used for comparing two or more
survival curves across different habitats. I hope this hint might help
in the analysis of your data.

REFERENCES:
1) LAING, S.E., BUCKLAND, S.T., BURNS, R.W., LAMBIE, D. & AMPHLETT,
A. (2003): Dung and nest surveys: estimating decay rates. Journal of
Applied Ecology, 40: 1102-111.
2) HOSMER, DAVID W. & STANLEY LEMESHOW (1999): Applied Survival
Analysis: regression modeling of time to event data. A
Wiley-Interscience Publication, John Wiley & Sons, New York.


M.Sivaram
Scientist
Kerala Forest Research Institute
Peechi
